cards.title: Digging canals turns up local minerals

questions.question: When a colonist digging a canal finds something, how should it show up?

options.label: Lump on the bank, letter first time (Recommended)
options.description: The ore drops beside the canal with a small message; the first find of each material on a map gets a letter. Buys: clear and cheap to build. Costs: the letters add up early on. Why: you see every find without being nagged.

options.label: Reveal a small seam
options.description: A little vein of the ore appears in rock next to the canal, to mine later. Buys: feels like real discovery. Costs: needs rock beside the canal, and adds deposits outside the abundance sheet.

options.label: Message only
options.description: The ore drops with a small message, never a letter. Buys: quietest. Costs: easy to miss a rare find.

questions.question: Should deeper canal cuts be able to find the deeper, rarer local minerals?

options.label: Yes, deep cuts reach deep minerals (Recommended)
options.description: Shallow and mid cuts find surface minerals; deep and superdeep cuts can also find what a deep drill would. Buys: a reason to dig deep. Costs: one more thing to balance. Why: matches how the deep drill already works.

options.label: No, every depth is the same
options.description: Same chance and same pool at every depth. Buys: simplest. Costs: depth means nothing for mining.

questions.question: In a biome with no minerals to find, what should canal digging turn up?

options.label: Nothing extra (Recommended)
options.description: Digging just digs. Buys: honest; a barren land is barren. Costs: digging there has no side reward. Why: chunks would clutter every canal for little value.

options.label: Chunks of local rock
options.description: Matches your quarry ruling. Buys: consistent with quarries. Costs: every long canal litters the bank with stone chunks.

cards.title: Sluice boxes and panning in rivers

questions.question: Most biomes in the draft mineral sheet hold no gold at all, so how should river gold work?

options.label: Separate river column in the sheet (Recommended)
options.description: Each biome gets its own 'what the rivers carry' numbers, apart from its veins, so a river can carry gold where the hills do not. Buys: real placer gold, still set per biome by you. Costs: one more column to review. Why: keeps the sheet in charge.

options.label: Pan what the land already holds
options.description: Rivers give the biome's own heavy minerals only. Buys: no new column. Costs: gold almost nowhere; most rivers give silver or nothing.

options.label: Gold in every river
options.description: A flat gold rate wherever a river runs. Buys: simplest, always works. Costs: breaks the local-materials ruling.

questions.question: Which mod should the sluice box and panning live in?

options.label: River Works (Recommended)
options.description: River Works already owns the river current, weirs and the shared fish stock these reuse; canal digging stays in FlowWorks. Buys: no mod reaching into another. Costs: the idea you asked for is split across two mods. Why: they are river buildings.

options.label: FlowWorks, needing River Works
options.description: All three ideas in FlowWorks. Buys: one place for 'digging and water work'. Costs: FlowWorks must depend on River Works to read the current.

options.label: Their own small mod
options.description: A 'Prospecting' mod holding sluice and panning. Buys: easy to switch off whole. Costs: one more mod to keep.

options.label: Mining (Recommended)
options.description: Miners pan, and canal digging already uses mining speed. Buys: works today, no new skill needed. Costs: miners get busier. Why: panning takes minerals from the ground, like mining.

options.label: Salvaging
options.description: The proposed new salvage skill. Buys: gives that skill more to do. Costs: that skill is not decided yet, and salvage means taking apart made things.

questions.question: How should a colonist be told where to pan?

options.label: A panning spot on the bank (Recommended)
options.description: Place a free spot beside shallow moving water; the colonist works from the dry bank. Buys: the river current never sweeps them away. Costs: one spot per place you want panned. Why: River Works shoves anyone standing in moving water.

options.label: A panning zone over the water
options.description: Paint shallow water like a fishing zone. Buys: familiar, covers a stretch at once. Costs: colonists stand in the current and get pushed downstream.
